identity.name: JYOTI RESINS & ADHESIVES LTD.
identity.industry: Specialty Chemicals / Wood Adhesives & Retail Distribution

summary.oneLiner: Jyoti Resins delivered record Q4 revenue (+18% YoY) driven by 16% volume growth and aggressive brand spending, signaling a shift from pure distribution to brand-led market share capture. However, rising receivables (150-160 days) and a 100% spike in key raw material (VAM) prices pose near-term margin and cash flow risks despite 60-70% price pass-through initiated in May.

one-line thesis: Jyoti Resins delivered record Q4 revenue (+18% YoY) driven by 16% volume growth and aggressive brand spending, signaling a shift from pure distribution to brand-led market share capture. However, rising receivables (150-160 days) and a 100% spike in key raw material (VAM) prices pose near-term margin and cash flow risks despite 60-70% price pass-through initiated in May.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Record quarter, +18% YoY (16% volume, ~2% price); EBITDA Margin: ~27% (steady, within guidance); PAT: Not explicitly broken out in transcript text but implied strong due to margin stability; Order Book: N/A (B2C/B2B2C model); Net Debt: Net Cash position (INR 140cr FDs vs INR 95cr carpenter bonus liability), though working capital tied up in receivables. One-offs: Significant increase in advertising spend (4% of sales) and receivables buildup due to new state entry.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 15-20% volume CAGR targeted for next 2-3 years to reach INR 500cr; Margin: Sustainable EBITDA band of 23-25% (Gross Margin ~65%); Order Inflow: Focus on tertiary offtake via carpenter engagement; Capex: Brownfield expansion completing in 1-2 quarters (capacity 2,000 -> 3,500 tons/month).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for B2C adhesive model; performance tracked via monthly volume run-rates (March hit >2,100 tons).
segment / subsidiary detail: Retail contributes ~94% of revenue; OEM segment currently ~6% with target to reach 15% in 2-3 years. Geographic mix shifting from Gujarat/Maharashtra stronghold to new states (UP, Delhi, WB, Odisha, Chhattisgarh).
growth verticals / optionality: Untapped market share in mature states (only ~1/3 retail outlets penetrated in Mumbai); expansion into 2 new states in May '26; OEM segment scaling in metro cities; long-term vision to reach INR 1,000-1,200cr revenue.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin target 65%; EBITDA target 23-25%. Pressure from VAM prices doubling (INR 75-80 to INR 160-180/kg); management passed through 60-70% of cost hike via price increases effective May 1st. Advertising intensity increasing from 4% to 6-7% of revenue.
capex / expansion: Brownfield expansion nearly complete (80% done), adding 1,500 tons/month capacity within 1-2 quarters. Greenfield projects contemplated for FY27-29. Funded via internal accruals.
capital allocation: Prioritizing reinvestment for growth (brand building, capacity, working capital). Maintaining ~15% dividend payout. No buybacks planned; cash held in FDs/Liquid funds to support expansion and cover INR 95cr carpenter bonus liability.
risks & watch-items: Working Capital: Receivable days stretched to 150-160 days (vs normal 120) due to new state entry; Raw Materials: VAM price volatility linked to crude/geopolitics; Competition: New capacity additions by peers in Gujarat; Demand: Potential short-term demand destruction from sharp price hikes, though management sees limited impact as adhesives are small % of total furniture cost.
management quality / tone: Optimistic and aggressive on market share capture; transparent about working capital stretch being a strategic choice for new market entry; confident in passing on raw material costs; focused on 'transformation journey' from distributor-led to brand-led model.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'carpenter bonus liability' of ~INR 95cr acts as a unique working capital feature, effectively an interest-free float from the channel that funds part of the cash balance. The company is deliberately stretching receivables in new states for 2-3 years to build relationships, accepting lower cash conversion temporarily for market share.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising VAM prices and need for continuous price pass-through | Unorganized Local Adhesive Manufacturers | loser | High | Lack pricing power and hedging capabilities to absorb 100% VAM spike, likely to lose share to branded players like Jyoti who can enforce price hikes. |
| Intensifying brand wars and trade marketing spend (6-7% of sales) | Regional/Niche Adhesive Brands | loser | Med | Jyoti's aggressive celebrity endorsement and loyalty program spend raises the barrier to entry, squeezing smaller regional players who cannot match the marketing intensity. |

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
